newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-CIGAR TO STAND AT COOLMORE STUD IN KENTUCKY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CIGAR TO STAND AT COOLMORE STUD IN KENTUCKY.

text.p: Ireland's Coolmore Stud said on Wednesday that it had negotiated a deal with Cigar's owner Allen Paulson which will see the American equine superstar stand at Ashford Stud, a subsidiary of Coolmore, in Kentucky.

Coolmore said in a statement the deal, which values Cigar at about $25 million, also involved Michael Tabor, a major international owner and breeder who already stands Kentucky Derby-Belmont winner Thunder Gulch at Ashford, becoming a partner in the horse.

"It is a great honour for Ashford to stand the best horse any of us can remember," said John Magnier of Coolmore Stud, which also includes ex-trainer Vincent O'Brien and leading owner Robert Sangster.

"Our interest in the horse began when Vincent O'Brien saw Cigar in Dubai and was deeply impressed by him," Magnier added. The inaugural Dubai World Cup earlier this year was among Cigar's biggest successes, while over four decades O'Brien proved himself one of the greatest trainers ever until his retirement in 1994. "Vincent considered Cigar to be an outstanding racehorse with the looks to match," Magnier said.
Paulson said the deal, which is subject to a veterinary examination and contract signing, would allow him to retain a significant share in Cigar.
"It will ensure that one of the best horses seen in America in modern times will be available to U.S. breeders," he added. "We plan to breed some of the best mares to him."
Cigar, the reigning Horse of the Year, was retired last week after he finished third in the Breeders' Cup on October 26.
He amassed earnings of almost $6.25 million, having won 19 of 33 career starts, including a record-equalling 16 straight wins.
It is expected Cigar will stand at stud for around $75,000 a time for 1997.
